body.heading: A change of state, not a chore
paragraphs: This is not exercise in disguise, though it is movement too. A reset walk is a deliberate change of state: different air, different sights, a body in motion, and a mind allowed to idle.
Ten to twenty minutes is usually enough. Leave the problem behind on purpose; you are not abandoning it, you are letting your attention cool down so you can return to it fresh.

body.heading: Make it a tool you reach for
paragraphs: Decide in advance what triggers a reset walk: the third reread of the same paragraph, the rising urge to send a grumpy message, the 3 p.m. fog. A pre-made decision is easier to act on than a fresh debate.
Have a default route that needs no planning, in daylight if you can. Come back, drink some water, and notice what the first task looks like now. Often it has quietly become smaller.

takeaway: When the day jams, walk around the block and let your mind cool down.
